newsitem.title: USA: Quaker says backs 1997 EPS range.
newsitem.headline: Quaker says backs 1997 EPS range.

text.p: Quaker Oats Co said Thursday it backs a current range of analysts' earnings estimates for 1997 of roughly $1.50 to $1.65 a share.

"I think the range right now of Wall Street is probably about $1.50 to $1.65 (a share) and we're basically comfortable with that," Margaret Eichman, vice president of investor relations, said on a teleconference.
Quaker Chairman William Smithburg said Quaker is committed to real earnings growth of at least 10 percent in 1997.
"We're going to try like crazy to do even better that that," he added.

Earlier, Quaker reported earnings for 1996 of $1.34 a share, up from $0.72 a share, excluding gains and charges in both years. Including gains and charges, 1996 earnings fell to $1.80 a share from $5.39 a year ago.
The company said supply chain initiatives, along with a major improvement in merchandising efficiency, resulted in more than $100 million in savings.
Quaker's net interest expense declined to $99.4 million for 1996, compared to $125.4 million in 1995. Overall debt declined to $1.56 billion at the end of 1996 from $1.76 billion at the end of 1995.
